clue.text: Ancient American good to meet news boss

parts.note: the boss of a newspaper is its editor, abbreviated ED

explanation.surface: An elderly American meets a decent newspaper chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ancient has lived or lasted a long time, which is to be old in years.

clue.text: Metalwork in posh bathroom around dressing room

indicators.note: dressing is clothing wrapped about something, so the reversed letters are wrapped around the room abbreviation
around here signals that the posh-plus-bathroom letters are turned round, read back to front

parts.note: U is the crossword letter for upper-class or posh
the loo is the British informal word for a toilet or bathroom

explanation.surface: Fancy metal fittings in a smart bathroom near the place you get changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing room' looks like one phrase, but 'dressing' is the wrapping signal and 'around' the turnaround signal, making OOLU.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names gilded bronze or brass used to decorate furniture, a classic kind of decorative metalwork.

clue.text: One who helps France to be free

indicators.note: to set letters free is to let them loose to form a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A patriotic supporter wants France to be liberated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks like the end of a political slogan, but it is the anagram signal for FRANCE TO BE.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron who gives money or assistance to a person or cause is a helper.

clue.text: Albatross? Eagle? Yes and no!

parts.note: albatross and eagle are both birds and both golf scores; the answer is a bird-word and a golf score, but a different score from those two, hence yes and no

explanation.surface: A puzzled birdwatcher can't decide which seabird or raptor they have spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf an albatross is three under par, an eagle two under, and the answer one under: same family of bird-named scores, but neither of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The golf term for one stroke under par on a hole, and also a childish word for a small bird.

clue.text: Roman has drink with Greek in perfect setting

indicators.note: in places the Greek abbreviation within the perfect letters
a setting holds a jewel, so the perfect letters hold the Greek ones

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or perfect, written with the figure 1 as the letter I
cola is a fizzy soft drink

explanation.surface: A Roman enjoys a soft drink with a Greek friend in an ideal location.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means first-class; 'in' and 'setting' together signal the container. The man was the Roman governor of Britain, father-in-law of Tacitus.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnaeus Julius, the general and governor of Britain, bore this name, so he is a Roman by example.

clue.text: Destroy Scottish island — no small island

indicators.note: no here means without, so the abbreviation is taken away from the island's name

parts.note: Islay is an island of the Inner Hebrides, famous for whisky
I is the abbreviation for island, a small or shortened island

explanation.surface: Someone vows to ruin a Scottish island, sparing no little islet.
explanation.walkthrough: ISLAY is a Hebridean island off Scotland's west coast; lose I and SLAY remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To slay is to kill violently, which is to destroy a living thing.

clue.text: One among seven hills in China coming to a point

parts.note: china plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, and a mate is a pal
a tine is a prong or point of a fork or antler

explanation.surface: A tour guide picks out one of the famous hills, with China arriving at a particular point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' means mate, from Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate), a London East End word game. The capital C disguises it as the country.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the central of the seven hills on which ancient Rome was built, site of imperial palaces.

clue.text: Smile brings some light

definitions.meaning: a ray or shaft of light

explanation.surface: A grin cheers things up a little.
explanation.definitionFit: To beam is to smile radiantly, and a beam is a narrow ray of light.

clue.text: Cruelly avenging leader in suspension from job

indicators.note: cruelly suggests treating the words roughly, so their letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boss viciously takes revenge, perhaps by suspending someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cruelly' reads as describing the leader, but it signals the anagram of AVENGING LEADER.
explanation.definitionFit: This British idiom is the period when an employee serving notice is paid but told to stay away from work.

clue.text: See 9
Resistance stops bird moving herd

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so the resistance letter is plugged into the bird

parts.note: a dove is a kind of pigeon
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Opposition halts a bird that is driving cattle along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resistance' feels political, but it is the physics symbol R.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a herd or flock of animals being driven along together by drovers.

clue.text: Legion retreats to hold remote rural station

indicators.note: to hold means to contain, so the reversed letters enclose the synonym for remote
retreats means goes back, so the synonym for legion is read backwards

parts.note: legion as in 'their number is legion' means countless, a myriad
remote means far away

explanation.surface: A military legion withdraws to defend a far-off country outpost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreats' turns MYRIAD into DAIRYM, which holds FAR. 'Legion' tempts as a Roman army, but it means a vast number.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm producing milk is an agricultural establishment, a station in the countryside sense.

clue.text: Drive going backwards so landing in rough

indicators.note: landing in means arriving inside, so the reversed letters go within the synonym for rough

parts.note: crude means rough or unrefined

indicators.note: going backwards says the synonym for so is read in reverse

parts.note: so and as both mean in this way or therefore, as in 'so far as' and 'as far as'

explanation.surface: A golfer's tee shot travels backwards and ends up in the rough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' and 'rough' paint a golf course, but the drive is a campaign; 'going backwards' and 'landing in' are the turnaround and container signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive is an organised campaign, and the answer is a vigorous campaign for a cause.

clue.text: Vessel crossing river brings chicken

indicators.note: crossing here means straddling, so the vessel sits either side of the river

parts.note: a can is a container or vessel
the Po is the longest river in Italy

explanation.surface: A boat crossing a river is carrying poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a boat to go with the river, but it is a container: CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a castrated cockerel fattened for the table, a type of chicken.

clue.text: Scar that reveals Satan?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, an aged cut or notch, which a scar is
a traditional nickname for the Devil

explanation.definitionFit: A long-standing English nickname for the Devil, and taken literally it is a cut from long ago.

clue.text: Discouragement as lower classes hear Latin dramatist

parts.note: D and E are the lowest grades in the British socio-economic classification

indicators.note: hear says the dramatist's name is taken as it sounds, not as spelt

parts.note: Terence was a Roman comic playwright

explanation.surface: Working-class audiences listen to a Roman playwright, which puts them off.
explanation.walkthrough: British market research grades households A to E, so DE means the lower classes. 'hear' makes TERENCE said aloud give the spelling TERRENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The act of putting someone off doing something by threat is discouragement.

clue.text: Is it taken up by chef in kitchen?

definitions.text: Is it taken up by chef in kitchen?

indicators.note: taken up says the hidden letters are read backwards
by here means beside or within, pointing to letters lodged inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A puzzled question whether something has been picked up by the cook.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden letters EFINK, found 'by' the words 'chef in kitchen', are reversed by 'taken up', upward in this down clue. The whole clue also defines: a cook's blade is exactly what one would take up.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting blade is the tool a chef most often picks up in a kitchen, so the question points to it.

clue.text: Shell in Aleppo detonates

indicators.note: in says the letters are found inside the following words, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A bomb shell goes off in the Syrian city of Aleppo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell' suggests artillery to suit the surface, but it is a pea's casing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pod is the outer case of peas and beans, the husk or shell around the seeds.

clue.text: Put down false name in legal document

indicators.note: in places the scrambled letters inside the legal document

parts.note: a deed is a signed legal document, such as a property deed

indicators.note: false means not genuine, so the letters of name are faked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone records a bogus name in an official paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'false' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container signal; 'Put down' means belittled, not written down.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone down is to belittle or humiliate them, lowering their dignity.

clue.text: Johnson in tribute offers high-level support for sailors

indicators.note: in places the Prime Minister's abbreviation inside the tribute

parts.note: a toast is a tribute drunk to someone
Boris Johnson was the UK Prime Minister, abbreviated PM

explanation.surface: Johnson raises a glass as a tribute to the navy's support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Johnson' could be Samuel Johnson or others; the Prime Minister fits the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the upper section of a ship's mast, a tall spar holding up sails and rigging.

clue.text: Doctored main polo mount

indicators.note: doctored means tampered with, so these letters are tampered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The chief polo pony has been drugged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mount' looks like a verb, but it is a horse one rides.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a golden horse with a pale mane, and a horse ridden is a mount.

clue.text: Folk above ground in Wells disowning old priest

indicators.note: disowning means casting off, so the old abbreviation is dropped from the folk's name

parts.note: in H.G. Wells's novel The Time Machine the Eloi live on the surface while the Morlocks live below

explanation.surface: Villagers in the cathedral city of Wells reject their elderly priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wells' looks like the cathedral city in Somerset, but it is the author H.G. Wells.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible names this man as priest of Shiloh, who brought up the prophet Samuel.

clue.text: Figure manure should be spread and left

indicators.note: manure is spread over fields, so its letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A farmer says the dung ought to be spread, with some left over.
explanation.definitionFit: A symbol for a number, such as a digit, is a figure.

clue.text: Documentary technique not about showing transport

indicators.note: not removes the letters for about from the documentary word

parts.note: reportage is the factual, journalistic style of reporting used in documentaries
re means about or concerning, as in letter headings

explanation.surface: A film-maker's method avoids depicting vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes RE out of REPORTAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means carrying boats or goods overland between waterways, and also the cost of carriage.

clue.text: Ten moving into flat — five in this group

indicators.note: into places the rearranged letters within the word for flat

parts.note: a pad is informal for a flat or apartment

indicators.note: moving means shifting about, so the letters of ten are shifted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Ten people move into an apartment, with five in each group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' makes ENT and 'into' is the container signal; 'flat' is slang for a pad.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a set or group of five, from the Greek for five.

clue.text: Heat can make a run grim

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
dour means stern, gloomy or grim

explanation.surface: Hot weather can turn a jog into an ordeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can make' is a link phrase; 'can' is not a tin here.
explanation.definitionFit: Passionate enthusiasm is heat in the figurative sense, intensity of feeling.

clue.text: See 27
Vicious for one English bank

parts.note: Sid Vicious was the Sex Pistols' bassist, an example of someone named Sid

explanation.surface: A cruel English bank, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vicious' is capitalised as a surname: Sid Vicious of the punk band the Sex Pistols.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank of a river is one of its edges, and edge is a common meaning of the answer.

clue.text: Work companion right when leaving cheesy village

indicators.note: when leaving means once these letters depart, so they are taken out of the village's name

parts.note: Cheddar is a Somerset village that gave its name to the cheese
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A colleague who is right leaves a village famous for cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when leaving' takes CH from the front and R from the end of CHEDDAR, a Somerset village that named the cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a medieval Icelandic collection of Norse myths and poems, a literary work.

clue.text: Wise politician deals cunningly with matters in short space

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the printer's space

parts.note: an en is a printer's space half the width of an em, so a short space

indicators.note: cunningly suggests craftily reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A seasoned politician shrewdly handles business in a tight timeframe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cunningly' makes LDERSTATESMA, which 'in' places within the printer's en. 'Short space' tempts as a short time, but it is a printing term.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a senior politician respected for experience and wisdom, often still consulted after leaving office.

clue.text: Rodent ultimately done for speed

parts.note: a rat is a rodent

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of done is taken

explanation.surface: A rat finally finished off, and quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means pace or velocity, as in 'at a fair old clip'.

clue.text: Awesome Rastafarian

definitions.meaning: a follower of Rastafari, short for one wearing dreadlocks

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means fearsome and awe-inspiring; as a noun it is slang for a Rastafarian with dreadlocks.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing turned on a cold nobleman

indicators.note: turned means reversed, so the word on is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a count is a European nobleman

explanation.surface: A worthless person attacks a chilly aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned on' looks like 'attacked', but 'turned' reverses ON to NO.
explanation.definitionFit: A worthless person of no importance is a ne'er-do-well, a good-for-nothing.
